title: "Configuration"

# Configuration {#sec-configuration}

All settings register with `CBA_fnc_addSetting` and appear in the CBA Settings menu under the **AEE** categories. Values marked *global* must match across all clients.

## AEE Armour → Armour

| Setting | Type | Default | Global | Addon | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aee_armour_armourEnabled` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | armour | Apply the STANAG 4569-aligned vehicle armour ladder (issue #126) |

## AEE Armour → Penetration

| Setting | Type | Default | Global | Addon | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aee_armour_penetrationDebug` | CHECKBOX | `false` | yes | armour | Log penetration gate decisions (round mm RHA vs protection) to the RPT |
| `aee_armour_penetrationGate` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | armour | Scale vehicle damage by the round's real RHA penetration vs the STANAG protection class - a rifle cannot shred an IFV |

## AEE Mobility → Hydrology

| Setting | Type | Default | Global | Addon | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aee_mobility_baseflowRate_perDay` | SLIDER | `0.2` | yes | mobility | Linear-reservoir recession rate per day for groundwater baseflow. USGS SIR 2022-5114 gives 0.9 to 0.99 per day for a perennial stream, which is this value as a daily retention. |
| `aee_mobility_bedSlope` | SLIDER | `0.001` | yes | mobility | Bed slope in metres per metre. Manning rating sets the stage from the discharge, and a steeper bed carries the same flow at a lower stage. |
| `aee_mobility_catchmentArea_m2` | SLIDER | `250000` | yes | mobility | Area in square metres draining to the river point. A river stage responds to everything upstream, so this is the contributing area rather than the routing cell. 250000 is a small stream catchment. |
| `aee_mobility_manningN` | SLIDER | `0.035` | yes | mobility | Manning roughness coefficient n for the channel. 0.030 to 0.050 is a natural stream (Chow 1959); 0.025 is smooth earth. |
| `aee_mobility_mudAccretionRate` | SLIDER | `0.002` | yes | mobility | Mud build-up rate per 5 s tick while driving on muddy terrain |
| `aee_mobility_mudDecayRate` | SLIDER | `0.99` | yes | mobility | Mud shedding factor per 5 s tick on hard surfaces (1 = no decay) |
| `aee_mobility_rainAccumDecay` | SLIDER | `0.97` | yes | mobility | Rain-history decay factor per 5 s tick (lower = faster drying) |
| `aee_mobility_riverResponseRate` | SLIDER | `0.1` | yes | mobility | Nash-cascade storage coefficient per 5 s tick; 1/k = reservoir time constant |
| `aee_mobility_riverSectionWidth_m` | SLIDER | `4` | yes | mobility | Width in metres of the modelled river section. Rising runoff is spread over a 100 m catchment cell and divided by this width to give the water-level rise. |
| `aee_mobility_tidalReach_m` | SLIDER | `5000` | yes | mobility | Distance in metres inland that the tide raises the river level. Full tidal amplitude at the coast, falling to zero at this distance. |

## AEE Mobility → Rollover

| Setting | Type | Default | Global | Addon | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aee_mobility_rolloverDynamicFactor` | SLIDER | `0.8` | yes | mobility | Fraction of the static threshold a manoeuvre reaches before the inside wheels lift. Published range 0.7 to 0.9 because body roll, tyre deflection and load transfer reduce the limit. 0.8 is the default. |
| `aee_mobility_rolloverEnabled` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | mobility | Tip a vehicle whose sustained lateral acceleration exceeds its Static Stability Factor threshold. The threshold is SSF = track width / (2 x centre-of-gravity height), corrected for ground slope (Gillespie). A single frame cannot roll a vehicle; the condition must hold. |
| `aee_mobility_rolloverHoldFrames` | SLIDER | `10` | yes | mobility | Frames the lateral acceleration must stay above the threshold before the vehicle rolls. A transient spike from a kerb or a collision must not roll it. Lower values roll more readily. |
| `aee_mobility_rolloverRadius` | SLIDER | `50` | yes | mobility | Distance in metres within which the rollover check runs. The candidate vehicle list is cached and refreshed every 5 seconds, so the loop does not scan the world every frame. |
| `aee_mobility_rolloverTorqueScale` | SLIDER | `0.25` | yes | mobility | Rotational impulse applied per sustained roll event, scaled by vehicle mass. The engine has no tilt command, so the roll uses addTorque at the centre of mass; the impulse must be sustained to overcome the solver. |

## AEE Mobility → Terrain

| Setting | Type | Default | Global | Addon | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aee_mobility_terrainDragEnabled` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | mobility | Slow a vehicle on rough or soft ground by applying a drag force opposing its motion. The force comes from a per-surface speed factor: road 1.00, field 0.40 to 0.55, woodland 0.25 to 0.40, sand 0.15 to 0.30, swamp 0.10 to 0.20. The engine has no command that caps a driven vehicle's speed, so a physical force is used, applied on the driver's machine. |
| `aee_mobility_terrainDragScale` | SLIDER | `0.3` | yes | mobility | Strength of the terrain drag force, per unit of overspeed above the surface's target speed, scaled by vehicle mass. A higher value pulls the vehicle to the target speed faster. The force is applied only above the target, so a slow vehicle is never dragged to a stop. |
| `aee_mobility_terrainRadius` | SLIDER | `50` | yes | mobility | Distance in metres within which the terrain drag check runs. The candidate vehicle list is cached and refreshed every 5 seconds, so the loop does not scan the world every frame. |

## AEE Mobility → Vehicle

| Setting | Type | Default | Global | Addon | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aee_mobility_estimateVehicleMassEnabled` | CHECKBOX | `false` | yes | mobility | Show a bounded mass estimate for a ground vehicle that the sourced catalogue does not cover. The estimate is modelled, not documented. It uses the vehicle box size, a cited material density, and a calibrated fill factor. The switch is off until calibration passes and a human approves the model. A sourced catalogue weight always takes precedence. The estimate never replaces a documented weight. |
| `aee_mobility_vehicleCouplingEnabled` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | mobility | Couple the computed surface physics to the engine at run time. Snow load adds mass with setMass, and a wet or icy surface removes grip with a force. The load comes from the modelled snow depth and the sourced snow density. No published accretion mass exists for mud, so mud adds no mass. The force is applied on the machine that owns the vehicle. |

## AEE Radio → Link

This category registers only when ACRE2 or TFAR is loaded. The radio
simulation feeds the ACRE2 and TFAR compat layers; without either host
mod its settings and computed state have no consumer, so they are not
registered.

| Setting | Type | Default | Global | Addon | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aee_radio_batteryDeratingEnabled` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | radio | Scale effective transmit power by the physiology battery temperature derating |
| `aee_radio_propagationRange` | SLIDER | `2.0` | yes | radio | Ceiling of the radio propagation quality index |
| `aee_radio_txPower` | SLIDER | `37` | yes | radio | Reference handheld transmit power in dBm used in the link budget |

| Setting | Type | Default | Global | Addon | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aee_thermal_repaintHz` | SLIDER | `4` | yes | thermal | Thermal selections repainted per second. The engine re-uploads a procedural texture for each one, and that cost lands on the render thread where no script timer sees it. The physics still solves every pass, so the image gain and every thermal coupling are unaffected. |
| `aee_thermal_thermalBaseChannel` | LIST | `0` | yes | thermal | The host channel for the thermal display. Vanilla TI runs the display on the engine's own thermal channel overlaid on the vehicle's native TI. DTV disables the vehicle's native TI and draws the display over the day channel instead, the route the proven A3TI and MKK thermal mods use, so the engine's TI pass cannot fight the mod's. DTV is vehicle-only: the player must be in a vehicle optic. It is a prototype for comparison and is the only channel that does not set the ppEffectForceInNVG flag. |
| `aee_thermal_thermalDisplayMode` | LIST | `0` | yes | thermal | Automatic follows the scene radiance histogram (AGC). Manual uses the fixed window below, like the level and span control on a real thermography or thermal weapon sight. Local normalises each object to its own selection range: it widens that object's internal contrast, but it breaks comparison between objects because a hot and a cold object can map to the same ramp. The local gain is capped at 8 times, so a flat object is not given invented contrast. |
| `aee_thermal_thermalFPN` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | thermal | Add fixed-pattern noise (static spatial mottle) over painted thermal objects - the perlinNoise detail stage real LWIR sensors show on top of the temporal FilmGrain. |
| `aee_thermal_thermalManualMaxC` | SLIDER | `120` | yes | thermal | Hot end of the manual display window, in degrees Celsius. Set it high to keep fires and exhaust on scale. The device library publishes no span, so this window is a user setting, not a device figure. |
| `aee_thermal_thermalManualMinC` | SLIDER | `-40` | yes | thermal | Cold end of the manual display window, in degrees Celsius. Used in manual display mode and as the fallback before the scene AGC is ready. The device library publishes no span, so this window is a user setting, not a device figure. |
| `aee_thermal_thermalPPEffects` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | thermal | Applies the five full-screen thermal effects: colour grade, black-hot inversion, sensor grain, IR-scatter blur and the ocular vignette. Turn OFF to isolate their render cost. |
| `aee_thermal_thermalPalette` | LIST | `0` | yes | thermal | Ember interpolates the engine's own decoded thermal colours through a continuous ramp. White hot grey is the luminance form of the same ramp. |
| `aee_thermal_thermalPolarity` | LIST | `0` | yes | thermal | White hot (hot = white) is the system default (AN/PAS-13 initialises white hot). Black hot (hot = black) is a user-selectable alternative - FM 3-22.9 states polarity is user preference |

## AEE → Core

| Setting | Type | Default | Global | Addon | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aee_core_computeMode` | LIST | `0` | yes | core | Where the environment computation runs. Deterministic (default): every machine computes the same values with NO network traffic. Costs the same CPU on server and clients, and is the only mode that cannot desynchronise. Server authority: the server computes and broadcasts the shared state each tick. Lowers client CPU at the cost of roughly 0.6 MB per minute per client at an 80 player count, and it needs a full resync when a player joins mid mission. Server map facts only: the server computes the once-per-mission terrain facts and every machine keeps its own position work. A few hundred bytes once, and it removes the only startup hitch on a large map. |
| `aee_core_diagnostic` | CHECKBOX | `false` | no | core | Enable verbose diagnostic logging (diag_log) for environment state changes |
| `aee_core_enabled` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | core | Master switch for the AEE environment simulation module |
| `aee_core_lightScanInterval` | SLIDER | `30` | yes | core | Seconds between dynamic light-source scans on the client. The contribution changes only when a lamp toggles or the weather attenuates it. 0 scans every tick. |
| `aee_core_logDebug` | CHECKBOX | `false` | yes | core | Log DEBUG and TRACE lines to the RPT. Values, not narration: each line carries the real inputs the code used. Off by default. |
| `aee_core_referenceAltitude` | SLIDER | `0` | yes | core | Override reference altitude (m MSL) for station pressure calculations. 0 = auto-detect from unit position |
| `aee_core_updateInterval` | SLIDER | `5` | yes | core | Simulation update interval in seconds (lower = more frequent updates) |

## AEE FX → Exhaust plume

Per-vehicle published values.  A mission or a mod sets these on a vehicle
object.  They are not CBA settings.

| Variable | Type | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aee_exhaustTier` | STRING | unset | Tier override, one of `land`, `heli`, `jet`, `ab`. Wins over the class selection |
| `aee_exhaustAfterburner` | BOOL | unset | A truthy value selects the afterburner tier, because no verified config key distinguishes an afterburning jet from a dry one |
| `aee_enginePowerFraction` | NUMBER | unset | Engine power fraction in 0..1. Overrides the real reader and the declared idle |
| `aee_engineRatedPowerW` | NUMBER | `150000` | Rated engine power in watts for the derived ground load. Overrides the declared default |
| `aee_exhaustGasTempC` | NUMBER | unset | Measured exhaust gas temperature in Celsius. Overrides the class row |
| `aee_exhaustPlumeM` | NUMBER | unset | Measured plume depth in metres. Overrides the class row |

The class row comes from the tier table in `fnc_applyExhaustShimmer.sqf`,
and `fnc_calculateExhaustPlume.sqf` interpolates it from the engine power
fraction.  The endpoints are declared defaults and not measurements.  When
no published value is set, the power fraction comes from the real reader,
`collectiveRTD` for a helicopter and `throttleRTD` for fixed wing, which is
gated on the advanced helicopter flight model and is unavailable when it is
off.  A land vehicle and a gated-off client use the declared idle fraction.


## AEE Optics → Intensity (historical)

The night-vision grain ceilings moved to the Night Vision addon and now
register as `aee_nightvision_nightGrainMax`, `aee_nightvision_rainGrainMax`
and `aee_nightvision_fogGrainMax`. The older names are kept here.

| Setting | Type | Default | Addon | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aee_optics_nightGrainMax` | SLIDER | `0.7` | optics | Night noise floor, the perceived darkness of night vision |
| `aee_optics_rainGrainMax` | SLIDER | `0.4` | optics | Rain-on-eye noise at night |
| `aee_optics_fogGrainMax` | SLIDER | `0.15` | optics | Fog haze grain added to the night grain effect |
